comment: Facts SatNOGS does not carry. Strength classes are reports from operators and amateurs, not measurements made by SignalHive; a transmitter listed under verifiedTransmitters has been received on air by the owner (none yet).

satellites.name: METEOR-M2 3
satellites.note: Its LRPT antenna did not fully deploy, so the signal is weak: only high passes with a good antenna work, and a simple mast antenna often gets nothing. (Operator and amateur reports; not measured here.)

satellites.name: METEOR-M2 4
satellites.note: LRPT downlink at 137 MHz, reported strong enough for a simple antenna on higher passes. (Amateur reports; not measured here.)

suppressedTransmitters.reason: NOAA 20: SatNOGS lists the GPS L2 frequency as a downlink; it is the satellite's GPS receiver, not a transmitter.
NOAA 20: SatNOGS lists the GPS L1 frequency as a downlink; it is the satellite's GPS receiver, not a transmitter.
